FSB Recruited Kyiv Teen on Telegram to Register 148 Starlinks for Russian Troops, SBU Says
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-15
08:22:01 UTC
17:22:01 KST

- Category
- War in Ukraine
FSB Recruited Kyiv Teen on Telegram to Register 148 Starlinks for Russian Troops, SBU Says
Ukraine’s Security Service (SBU) detained an alleged Federal Security Service (FSB) agent in Kyiv who attempted to activate 148 Starlink terminals for Russia, the SBU reported on October 14.
According to the SBU, the operation prevented one of the largest known batches of Starlink satellite terminals from being registered for Russian use. The agency stated that Russian forces intended to use the terminals to plan combat operations in the Donetsk and Zaporizhzhia regions.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
Starlink has become central to Ukrainian combat operations, providing satellite connectivity for command links, real-time drone video, artillery coordination, and unmanned strike missions. Ukrainian forces have also used Starlink-connected drones for medium-range attacks on Russian logistics, while Kyiv has sought expanded access to support deeper strikes against military targets.
Investigators identified the suspect as an 18-year-old former student at a Kyiv college who had trained as a welder. The SBU stated that he was recruited after searching Telegram channels for quick ways to earn money.
According to the investigation, an FSB officer contacted the teenager through one of the chats and offered him payment in exchange for cooperation.
The SBU reported that within several days of his recruitment, the suspect registered 15 Starlink terminals using the passport details of relatives and acquaintances.
Investigators stated that he then prepared false personal data to register another 133 terminals for the Russian security service.
Counterintelligence officers detained the suspect near a post office as he allegedly prepared to activate another batch of Starlink terminals. The SBU also blocked terminals that had already been registered after the suspect transmitted their credentials to his Russian handler through a messaging app.
Several smartphones containing what investigators described as evidence of his cooperation with Russia were seized during searches.
The suspect was notified of suspicion under Part 2 of Article 111 of Ukraine’s Criminal Code, covering high treason committed under martial law.
He remains in custody without the right to bail and faces life imprisonment with confiscation of property if convicted.
Earlier on October 14, Ukrainian forces reported disruptions to Starlink-based battlefield communications that forced some drone units to cancel missions. The restrictions affected Starshield connections used to control unmanned aircraft, with Ukrainian troops reporting signal losses during flight.

Ukraine and Moldova Draft Energy Deal on Gas, Power, and Fuel Before Winter
Ukraine and Moldova are preparing a bilateral agreement to solidify future energy cooperation following talks on October 14 between Ukrainian Energy Minister Denys Shmyhal and Moldovan Prime Minister Vasile Tofan.
The discussions focused on joint energy challenges, winter preparation, and natural gas transit through a shared pipeline corridor, according to Denys Shmyhal.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
The two nations are also exploring options for Ukraine to import additional volumes of electricity during Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
“One of the key topics is passing the winter period. Ukraine and Moldova face common challenges in the operation of power systems and the issue of natural gas supply. Therefore, we primarily discussed the transportation of natural gas through a shared gas corridor and the possibilities of importing additional volumes of electricity,” Shmyhal noted.
Beyond grid operations and gas corridors, the officials coordinated steps to resolve operational concerns on the Dniester River and accelerate fuel transit through Moldova.
Measures include shortening tank truck border queues to secure swift fuel supplies to Ukraine.
“We separately raised the issue of simplifying procedures at the Ukrainian-Moldovan border. We discussed the implementation of joint control practices at checkpoints and the organization of corresponding bilateral consultations,” the energy minister added.
During the Moldova Security Forum in Chișinău on October 8, Moldovan President Maia Sandu announced that her country was prepared to host additional displaced Ukrainians if winter conditions severely deteriorated.
She noted that over 1 million Ukrainians had crossed into Moldova since the start of Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, with approximately 100,000 remaining in the country.
Meanwhile, Dorin Recean, Special Envoy to the President, confirmed that Chișinău was coordinating energy assistance for Ukraine, highlighting that while Moldova could not generate enough power to export directly, electricity could be transit-shipped through Moldovan territory from Romania.

Germany’s rail operator bans alcohol at all train stations
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-15
08:21:49 UTC
17:21:49 KST

Ayhan Simsek
15 October 2026•Update: 15 October 2026
Germany’s national rail operator Deutsche Bahn has banned alcohol consumption at all its train stations in a bid to improve passenger safety and cleanliness.
The rule, introduced Thursday under the company’s house regulations, covers public station areas under Deutsche Bahn control, including platforms. Station restaurants remain exempt, and passengers may continue to carry sealed alcoholic drinks in bags. Alcohol is generally still allowed on trains.
At train stations, security personnel will enforce the rule during regular patrols. Those who ignore the ban may face immediate removal from the area. Repeat violators could face longer bans from station premises.
The company described the measure as a response to suggestions from passengers, employees and others seeking safer and cleaner stations. Deutsche Bahn said a recent representative survey found that 79% of respondents supported the ban on alcohol consumption at train stations, while only 9% opposed it.

In Germany, AfD and BSW called for an end to military aid to Ukraine

In Germany, AfD and BSW called for an end to military aid to Ukraine
Kyiv • UNN
The AfD and BSW parties jointly adopted a resolution against military aid to Ukraine in Saxony-Anhalt. The document has no practical consequences.
The far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party and the small left-wing BSW party joined forces on Wednesday, October 14, to pass a resolution in the parliament of the German state of Saxony-Anhalt calling for Berlin to end its military support for Ukraine. Reuters reports, UNN writes.
Details
Germany, led by Chancellor Friedrich Merz, remains one of the key suppliers of military aid to Ukraine in Europe. The federal government has repeatedly confirmed its intention to continue supporting Kyiv. At the same time, the AfD and BSW oppose military aid, arguing that ending it would allow more funds to be directed toward the country’s domestic needs.
The vote in Saxony-Anhalt will not have a direct impact on Germany’s foreign policy, as state parliaments do not determine the extent of military support for Ukraine. However, the political significance of this decision goes beyond the issue of aid to Kyiv itself: it could become a prerequisite for forming new parliamentary majorities in the region.
According to the publication, last month the Alternative for Germany party won the election in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt, but it fell short of the votes needed for an absolute majority in the state parliament. Siegmund said that by the end of the year he plans to seek approval as the region’s prime minister. At the same time, other parties have ruled out forming a coalition with the AfD. They adhere to the so-called "firewall" policy, which entails the political isolation of this party.
It will be recalled
German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil stated his unwavering support for Ukraine and expectations of political reforms. The EU is seeking additional funding.

Cactus Club in Oudergem closes after 40 years: “Partying in nightclubs is out of fashion”
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-15
08:21:00 UTC
17:21:00 KST

The Cactus Club in Oudergem (Brussels) is closing for good on 2 January. After 40 years of partying, the nightclub wants to call it a day whilst it’s still at the top of its game. “The years ahead would look catastrophic,” says owner Philippe Harlet.
Cactus Club in Oudergem closes after 40 years: “Partying in nightclubs is out of fashion”
Party-goers in the south of Brussels will soon have one club fewer to choose from. The Cactus Club is closing because it takes a bleak view of the future. “We want to end on a high rather than face catastrophic years ahead,” says owner Philippe Harlet.
The club emphasises that the closure is not due to financial difficulties. However, Harlet has noticed a gradual decline in visitor numbers. “Fewer and fewer people want to party in a nightclub,” says Harlet. “They prefer a bar or a café.”
Cactus Club revellers mainly come from municipalities in the south of Brussels. “Tourists struggle to find their way here from the Brussels downtown. That’s always been the case. So, the location was never an obstacle to filling our club.”
From 2027, a ban on smoking and vaping will apply on all outdoor terraces. Public smoking rooms will also be banned. “That’s going to have a major impact,” says Harlet. “Party-goers will no longer be able to use our indoor smoking room.”
Club history
With 24 evenings still to come, the Cactus Club will not let its final months pass quietly. On 10 November, it will celebrate its 40th anniversary. On 2 January, a final party takes place, marking the end of four decades of club history.
Afterwards, the building on Vorstlaan in Oudergem will be put up for sale. “The asking price is not yet known, but I hope it will be put to good use,” concludes Harlet.
Brussels’ nightlife has been under severe pressure for some time now. Nightclubs Spirito in Elsene and La Cabane in Watermaal-Bosvoorde were forced to close last year.

CBA season preview: Reforms fuel title race, reignite relegation battle
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-15
16:15:59 CST
17:15:59 KST

by sportswriter Cao Yibo
BEIJING, Oct. 15 (Xinhua) -- The 2026-27 Chinese Basketball Association (CBA) season tips off on Friday, with changes to the competition format, a reshuffled title race and expanded opportunities for young players set to shape the campaign.
The league's 32nd season will see promotion and relegation return after more than two decades, the regular season expand to 46 rounds and foreign-player registration limits tightened. Beyond the regular season, the CBA Club Cup and the Chinese Basketball Development League (CBDL) will also provide additional opportunities for competition and player development.
REFORMS RAISE STAKES FOR CLUBS
The 2026-27 CBA regular season will feature 460 games across 46 rounds, up from 420 last season. The playoffs will return to a 3-5-5-7 format, replacing last season's 3-3-5-7 system. The round of 12 will remain a best-of-three series, while the quarterfinals and semifinals will be played in a best-of-five format, followed by a best-of-seven final.
The most notable structural change this season is the return of promotion and relegation, which was abandoned after the 2003-04 season.
The bottom two CBA teams after the regular season will face the top two sides from the National Basketball League (NBL) in home-and-away playoffs in April 2027. Winners must still pass salary-cap compliance checks and a subsequent admission assessment to register for the following CBA season.
Overseas-player regulations have also been tightened. Each club may register up to three overseas players at a time, down from four last season, with a season-long registration limit of six players, compared with eight previously. The salary cap will also shift from a fixed seasonal limit to a tiered system linked to a team's progress through the season.
The changes are expected to encourage more selective recruitment and give domestic players greater responsibility, but whether they lead to more competitive games and better development opportunities for Chinese players will be one of the season's central questions.
OFFSEASON RESHUFFLE SETS UP COMPETITIVE TITLE RACE
A series of offseason moves has reshaped the title race, with the Shanghai Sharks seeking to defend their crown and the Beijing Ducks, Shanxi Loongs, Zhejiang Lions and Guangdong Southern Tigers among the clubs looking to challenge.
Shanghai enters the season with much of its domestic core intact, including Zhang Zhenlin, Li Hongquan and Liu Zheng, while retaining last season's Finals MVP Brandon Goodwin. Former NBA All-Star D'Angelo Russell and NBA champion JaVale McGee have joined the squad, adding considerable experience and new offensive options.
Head coach Lu Wei, however, has stressed that last season's title cannot guarantee future success. "Since the final buzzer, the championship has already turned the page," he said, adding that the team must start over and approach each game with full commitment. How quickly Russell adapts to the CBA and fits into the team could be decisive in Shanghai's bid to defend the crown.
The Ducks are also looking to take the next step after reaching the semifinals last season. The club has brought in Barry Brown Jr., JaKarr Sampson and Lindy Waters III. Former Chinese national team coach Li Nan, who replaced Chinese basketball Hall of Famer Xu Limin, has called for a more forceful approach, particularly in defense and rebounding. "Results in competitive sport are not achieved by talk; they are fought for," he said at the team's season launch.
The Lions, meanwhile, will rely on continuity among key players Hu Jinqiu, Sun Minghui and Zhu Junlong, but must compensate for the departures of several domestic rotation players, including Zhao Jiaren and Lin Bingsheng. The club retained American scorer Rayjon Tucker, added Cameroon international Landry Nnoko and brought veteran Dezmine Wells back into the fold.
Shanxi, Zhejiang's opponent in the season opener, has made substantial changes after finishing 10th in the regular season and reaching the quarterfinals. The team retained import Hamidou Diallo and added Lindell Wigginton and Petr Cornelie. Domestic recruits Zhao Jiaren, Wang Junjie and Xie Zhijie are expected to strengthen the team's wing and backcourt rotations. A coaching change, with former assistant Vytautas Buzas taking charge, adds another variable as Shanxi seeks to build on its playoff run.
Eleven-time champion Guangdong has reinforced its overseas-player group with the additions of veteran guard Kyle Fogg and center Udoka Azubuike, alongside Croatian forward Luka Bozic. The availability of shooting guard Edmond Sumner, who has been dealing with a hand injury, could affect the team's early-season options.
The Beijing Royal Fighters, who narrowly missed the playoffs last season, have also undergone a significant rebuild. The Royal Fighters have appointed a new coaching staff led by head coach Charalampos Markopoulos, brought back forward Wang Shaojie and added Zhao Jiayi. Guard Grant Riller remains with the team and is joined by Harry Giles and Javonte Cooke. The club has set its sights on returning to the playoffs and challenging for a top-eight finish, although the new lineup will need time to build chemistry.
CLUB CUP AND YOUTH LEAGUE BROADEN STAGE
The CBA's competition structure will extend beyond the regular season. The third CBA Club Cup will return during the league's window periods, with 24 teams taking part: all 20 CBA clubs and four NBL teams. Group-stage games will be held in Wuhan, Yantai, Yinchuan and Qionghai, with the finals in Nanning. The expanded field and regional venues are intended to bring professional basketball to more cities and broaden the league's reach.
The CBDL will also expand, with all 20 CBA clubs fielding teams made up of players aged 18 to 24 from club rosters and youth squads. The league will feature 292 games across preliminary and final stages, providing young players with more opportunities to gain competitive experience.
The 2027 CBA All-Star Weekend will take place in Xi'an, Shaanxi Province, from March 5 to 7, marking the first time the event has been held in northwest China.
At the season launch, Chinese Basketball Association president Guo Zhenming said the national team's results still fell short of expectations.
"The league is the national team's most fundamental talent base and competitive platform. The two are closely linked and share the same destiny," he said. ■

TOKYO, Oct. 15 (Xinhua) -- Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said Thursday she has offered ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) lawmaker Arata Takebe the post of farm minister to succeed Kazuo Yana, who stepped down a day earlier in what was effectively a dismissal over a string of scandals, Kyodo News reported.
Takebe will be joining the cabinet for the first time.
The 56-year-old is a sixth-term House of Representatives lawmaker for a constituency on Japan's northernmost main island of Hokkaido.
He previously served as senior vice minister of agriculture, forestry and fisheries and director of the LDP's Agriculture and Forestry Division, among other posts.
Takebe's father, Tsutomu Takebe, held posts including farm minister and LDP secretary general.

It was also reported that he had provided free shuttle bus rides to his supporters during past lower house election campaigns, possibly in violation of the Public Offices Election Act.
Yana submitted his resignation at a meeting with Takaichi on Wednesday night, and the prime minister accepted it.
Analysts said Takaichi chose Takebe, who is well-versed in agricultural policy and administration, in a bid to minimize the impact of Yana's resignation on parliamentary deliberations and the running of her government.
However, Kyodo News said opposition parties are preparing to press Takaichi over her responsibility for appointing Yana, a move expected to weigh on her administration going forward. ■

First World War Soldier of the West Yorkshire Regiment Buried in France more than a century after his death
United Kingdom
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-15
09:15:33 BST
17:15:33 KST

First World War Soldier of the West Yorkshire Regiment Buried in France more than a century after his death
An unknown soldier of the West Yorkshire Regiment, discovered near the Thiepval Memorial on the Somme, has been given a peaceful burial more than 100 years after his death.
More than a century after his death in the First World War, the remains of a man of the West Yorkshire Regiment were laid to rest today (14 October 2026) with full military honours at the Commonwealth War Graves Commission’s (CWGC) Serre Road Cemetery No.2 in France.
In the winter of 2025 – 2026 human remains were discovered on the edge of a freshly ploughed field about a kilometre south of the Thiepval Memorial. Since the remains had been disturbed by a plough, it was impossible to fully understand the context of the find and to relate the artefacts to the soldier conclusively. However, a shoulder title found near the remains indicated possible service with the West Yorkshire Regiment, and this was strengthened by the presence of a belt with the letters WYR marked on it, also found near the casualty. An entrenching tool issued prior to July 1916 and first-issue webbing gave some clues as to when this soldier might have been equipped, but there was no clue as to his personal identity.
The recovery location was immediately adjacent to the Leipzig Redoubt, and records of the West Yorkshire Regiment show that various battalions were tasked with capturing Thiepval including the Leipzig Salient on the 1st July 1916, and remained in the line in this area until 17 July, before revisiting the area again in August of the same year.
Research showed that more than 1000 men of the West Yorkshire Regiment are named on the Thiepval Memorial, having died in the period 1 July 1916 – 31 August 1916. A further 745 men of the same regiment died on other dates from September 1915 to March 1918, and also remain missing.
With such an extensive list of potential candidates, and nothing in the way of artefactual evidence to point to his identity it proved impossible to identify the man. Nonetheless, he gave his life in the service of his country, fighting for freedom and peace. Whilst his identity remains known only to God, today he was buried by a party from the Royal Yorkshire Regiment – his military family, with full military honours.
The service was organised by the JCCC and supported by serving soldiers of the Royal Yorkshire Regiment, as well as staff from the CWGC.

Japan to halt Onagawa nuclear reactor over water leak
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-15
08:05:55 UTC
17:05:55 KST

Faisal Mahmud
15 October 2026•Update: 15 October 2026
Japan will suspend operations at a nuclear reactor in the country’s northeast around Saturday after detecting a leak of water containing a small amount of radioactive material, the plant’s operator said Thursday.
Tohoku Electric Power Co. said the No. 2 reactor at the Onagawa nuclear power plant in Miyagi Prefecture would be shut down to inspect and replace faulty components, according to Kyodo News.
The company said a small amount of radioactive material was detected in the leaking water, but all contaminated water had been collected.
No abnormal radiation levels were detected in the surrounding environment, it added.
The operator estimated that approximately 0.2 metric tons of water had been leaking every hour.
Water levels in a drainage sump had been rising since July, prompting an investigation that identified a leaking valve.
The company said inspections, repairs and preparations for restarting the reactor would take approximately 10 days.
The Onagawa reactor became the first in eastern Japan to resume operations after the devastating 2011 earthquake and tsunami triggered the Fukushima nuclear disaster.
The reactor was briefly shut down in November 2024, just days after restarting, because of equipment problems. It resumed operations later that month following repairs.
The 2011 disaster forced Japan to suspend nuclear operations nationwide and introduce stricter safety requirements before allowing reactors to restart.

Unprecedented rainfall triggers flash floods in Istanbul
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-15
08:00:33 UTC
17:00:33 KST

A spell of exceptionally intense precipitation across Türkiye’s Marmara region has broken historic meteorological records, delivering an unprecedented volume of rainfall to the metropolis of Istanbul within a remarkably brief window.
The storm generated localised rainfall figures rarely witnessed in the region's recorded climate history.
Meteorological measuring stations across the Marmara basin recorded extreme cloudbursts that shattered seasonal averages. In several Istanbul districts, precipitation levels exceeded 100 to 130 millimetres per square metre within just a few hours — a volume equivalent to nearly two months' worth of average autumn rainfall hitting the ground at once.
The sudden volume of water overwhelmed municipal drainage networks, causing underpasses, underground passages, and low-lying ground-floor properties to submerge rapidly.
While the entire Marmara region experienced heavy precipitation, Istanbul bore the brunt of the storm's impact, with several neighbourhoods experiencing critical damage.
In response to the escalating situation, central authorities in Ankara deployed state resources to coordinate emergency management and relief operations across the Marmara region.
The Disaster and Emergency Management Authority (AFAD) was immediately mobilised to direct field operations, dispatching high-capacity water evacuation pumps, search and rescue personnel, and amphibious vehicles to support Istanbul's emergency teams.
National meteorological authorities issued high-level weather alerts urging citizens to avoid unnecessary travel and remain indoors as municipal teams worked around the clock to clear debris and pump out submerged infrastructure.

Inside Nepal’s unending cycle of avalanches, floods and landslides
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-15
08:00:05 UTC
17:00:05 KST

Inside Nepal’s unending cycle of avalanches, floods and landslides
Experts warn such events could become an ‘annual occurrence’ and urge the government to rethink its development model
The rock-ice avalanche near the Nepal-Tibet border that opened the floodgates in the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli rivers on August 26 killed more than 1,450 people, with nearly 6,000 others still missing. It was followed by a massive landslide after parts of a mountain collapsed into a river in the Mustang region in late September.
And on Sunday, another rock-ice avalanche flooded the Budhi Gandaki River – which joins the Trishuli downstream – in central Nepal’s Gorkha district, with concrete-like slush swallowing houses, bridges and trekking trails, though no casualties were reported.
“To have two similar events, nearby and in one year, is unprecedented in Nepal,” said John Pomeroy, director of the Centre for Hydrology at Canada’s University of Saskatchewan, who has been following the events.
“While climate change did not directly trigger these catastrophes, the thawing of frozen ground, melt of glaciers, increased lubrication of frozen materials from rapid snowmelt and rainfall all destabilised the high mountains and created the preconditions that permitted these events to form.”

Boxer ruled out of cavalry role as variants shelved
United Kingdom
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-15
08:59:29 BST
16:59:29 KST

Armoured mortar, repair and recovery, and mounted close combat overwatch capabilities are no longer being pursued within the Mechanised Infantry Vehicle programme, and Boxer will not be used in the armoured cavalry role at all, according to answers given in Parliament.
Ben Obese-Jecty, the Conservative member for Huntingdon, asked what elements had been cut from the programme as part of the funding removal and budget reprioritisation recorded in the National Infrastructure and Service Transformation Authority’s Major Projects Annual Report for 2025 to 2026, which logged £1,858.38 million coming out. He separately asked how many of each Boxer variant would go to the armoured cavalry role and how many to mechanised infantry.
Luke Pollard, the Minister for Defence Readiness and Industry, said: “As part of reprioritisation within the Military Strategic Headquarters, the Armoured Mortar, Repair and Recovery and Mounted Close Combat Overwatch capabilities of the Mechanised Infantry Vehicle programme are no longer being pursued.
“The Army is considering how the underlying capability requirements will be addressed.”
On the cavalry question, Pollard said: “Boxer vehicles will not be used in the Armoured Cavalry role. Boxer will form the spine of the Mechanised Infantry force. Under current plans, Boxer is being fielded in supporting roles across 3rd (UK) Division, including Command and Control, Specialist Troop Carrier and Medical functions. Detailed fielding plans and vehicle allocations remain subject to refinement.”
The requirement survives the first decision even though the Boxer-based route to meeting it does not, which leaves the Army to find another way. In practice that means an existing vehicle takes the task on, a separate procurement follows, or the capability thins.
Each of the shelved functions does a job the mechanised infantry brigades still need done. Armoured mortar gives a battlegroup indirect fire of its own, able to move with the vehicles it supports and put rounds down without waiting on artillery allocated at a higher level. Repair and recovery keeps a wheeled armoured fleet running and drags disabled vehicles off the battlefield, which matters because a vehicle of Boxer’s weight that loses mobility cannot be moved by anything smaller than a purpose-built recovery variant. Mounted close combat overwatch is the anti-armour role, carrying a missile system that lets the infantry hold tanks at a distance.
Armoured cavalry is the reconnaissance and screening job the Army is equipping with Ajax, the tracked family built by General Dynamics Land Systems UK and fitted with a stabilised 40mm cased telescoped cannon. Ajax carries the sensors and the gun for that work, while Boxer is wheeled, has no turret on the British variants ordered so far, and is built to carry infantry and the things infantry need. Ruling it out of the role closes off a line of speculation that has followed the vehicle since Britain rejoined the programme.
Boxer is a modular design built around a common drive module onto which different mission modules are fitted, the feature that was supposed to make adding variants straightforward. Britain rejoined the programme in 2018, having left it in 2003, and the order has grown past six hundred vehicles across infantry carrier, specialist carrier, command and ambulance types, built under licence by Rheinmetall BAE Systems Land at Telford and WFEL at Stockport.

Trump press secretary Zacharia failed US bar exam despite claiming to practice law - report
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-15
07:58:58 UTC
16:58:58 KST

White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia did not pass a US bar exam, despite President Donald Trump describing her as an attorney when announcing her appointment, the Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday.
Zacharia took the California bar exam after graduating from Pepperdine University’s law school in 2011 but failed, a person with direct knowledge of the matter told the WSJ. At the time, she was preparing for her wedding and a move to China, the person added.
Questions about her credentials emerged after searches of attorney directories in California, Texas, and Washington, DC, under both her married and maiden name produced no listings.
Zacharia has claimed she is a lawyer on multiple occasions. When reporters asked her on Tuesday which state’s bar exam she had passed, she replied: “When I moved to China.”
Her LinkedIn profile currently lists her as having a Juris Doctor degree. Notably, if she did not pass the bar exam and has not been licensed, she is not a lawyer by definition.
Fox News also identified her as an attorney at least 18 times when she appeared as a commentator on several different programs. The network did not respond to the WSJ’s request for comment.
Zacharia has also called herself an attorney on other podcasts, news broadcasts, and media appearances.
In a statement, she said: “I practiced international transaction law, with all the appropriate credentials.”
Zacharia joined Beijing's Zhong Lun Law Firm in 2011
Zacharia moved to Beijing in the summer of 2011 and joined the international practice team at Zhong Lun Law Firm. A source familiar with her employment told the WSJ that she was among four international associates who drafted agreements for multimillion-dollar cross-border transactions and communicated with American and multinational clients operating in China.
Another source with direct knowledge of the matter said lawyers later advised Zacharia that her law degree and international transaction experience qualified her to provide legal analysis.
Her LinkedIn profile also lists a position as general counsel at Fix California, the nonprofit founded by Trump administration official Richard Grenell, from January 2024 to March 2025. General counsel positions usually involve serving as an organization's in-house lawyer, meaning Zacharia would have had to practice law, though she is not licensed to do so.
Acting as an organization’s attorney in California without a license would be a misdemeanor.
Someone familiar with her work there said she coordinated the organization’s outside lawyers and served as their point of contact.
Corinne Baum contributed to this report.

Alexandros Paporakis, 19, of Palatine, was arrested on Sunday after an individual reported receiving concerning electronic communications from him, Palatine police said on Wednesday. It was not immediately clear whether he had legal representation.
Detectives searched Paporakis’s home and recovered a rifle, multiple loaded rifle magazines and hundreds of additional rounds of rifle ammunition.
“Among the recovered items was a tactical vest containing body armor and a patch displaying imagery associated with white supremacist extremism,” a police statement said.
Paporakis’s coworker reportedly told police that he openly identified himself as a white supremacist at work and said he “couldn’t wait” to kill Indian people, according to prosecutors from the Cook County State’s Attorney’s office.
Detectives recovered a document called “Why I fought: A.K.A.: (Aurora Shooter’s Manifesto)” which had sentiments expressing white supremacist and extremist ideologies, referencing violence towards South Asians, specifically Indians.
Authorities believed Paporakis was planning to carry out his attack on Sunday, possibly targeting a Hindu temple in Aurora, 40 miles (65km) southwest of Palatine.
“However, the specific intended location has not been confirmed and remains under investigation,” the police said, adding the FBI was assisting in the probe.
Police said Paporakis is facing felony charges of “making a terrorist threat” and possessing an unlawful weapon.
The suspect appeared for a detention hearing on Wednesday and his next court appearance is scheduled for the end of October.
Human rights advocates said hate against South Asians has surged in the United States in recent years due to rising anti-immigration policies and a rise in white supremacist ideology.

Unknown Publisher

07:54:00 UTC
16:54:00 KST

A school roof collapse in the northwestern Pakistani city of Peshawar killed 32 pupils and a teacher Thursday, a hospital official said.
Twenty more students were taken to hospital after the collapse, which authorities blamed on "weak infrastructure." Others in the densely populated neighborhood described a close call.
Resident Sohail told Agence France-Presse (AFP) "everyone began screaming in panic" after his niece managed to find her way home after escaping the building to inform them of the collapse.
"When I arrived at the scene, I saw around 10 to 15 children trapped beneath the rubble, with debris piled up to their necks. We quickly pulled them out," he said.
Asim Khan of Peshawar's Lady Reading Hospital said the death toll had risen to 33 by Thursday evening, with most of the victims aged between four and 14.
"A total of 20 injured children were brought to the hospital, most of whom have been discharged. Three severely injured children, who sustained head injuries, have been admitted to the hospital," Khan said.
The injured and deceased included 12 girls and a female teacher, Khan added.
A spokesman for the emergency rescue service in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province said schoolchildren were crushed and trapped after the roof gave way.
"When the Rescue 1122 emergency response teams arrived at the scene, they found that one roof had collapsed onto another, causing the classroom below to be crushed and trapping children inside," spokesman Bilal Ahmad Faizi said.
Dozens of people were at the scene.
Images released by the emergency services showed rescue workers in high-visibility vests scrambling to move debris, rubble and dirt.
A senior Peshawar-based official said that initial reports suggested the roof collapse was due to "weak infrastructure."
"The school owner has been detained," the official said on condition of anonymity because he was not authorized to talk to the media.
Bodies wrapped in white cloth were seen being carried out of the hospital as volunteers arrived to help identify the victims.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressed "deep sorrow and grief over the loss of precious lives," according to a statement.
"The Prime Minister extends his condolences to the bereaved families and prays for them to have the strength and patience to bear this irreparable loss," the statement said.
President Asif Ali Zardari described the roof collapse as a "heartbreaking tragedy."
Resident Sher Ahmed blamed "substandard construction materials" for the tragedy and called for an investigation.
"With profound grief and sorrow, I urge the authorities to conduct a thorough investigation and take strict action against anyone found responsible so that such tragedies can be prevented in the future," he said.
Roof and building collapses are common in Pakistan, largely due to poor safety standards and substandard construction materials in the South Asian nation of more than 240 million people.
In June, more than a dozen children were killed when a roof collapsed at a tutoring center in the eastern city of Lahore.
In 2025, 27 people were killed and 10 injured when a five-story building collapsed in the impoverished Lyari area of the southern city of Karachi.

Two vessels caught fire near Romania: one may have been hit by drone, eight people are missing from the other

Unknown Publisher

Two vessels caught fire near Romania: one may have been hit by drone, eight people are missing from the other
Kyiv • UNN
A fire broke out on the San Marino-flagged vessel Wide Trader near Sulina. Four people have been rescued, while the search for eight others is still underway.
Romania said that eight people went missing after a fire broke out on a San Marino-flagged vessel on the morning of Thursday, October 15. It is the latest incident in the Black Sea, where a series of drone attacks has been carried out, Euronews reports, writes UNN.
Details
The vessel, named Wide Trader, reported a fire at around 7:00 a.m. local time, approximately 13 nautical miles southeast of the Romanian city of Sulina, according to a press release from the Romanian Naval Authority.
"There were 12 people on board the vessel. Four of them are safe, while eight are currently considered missing," the statement added.
A search-and-rescue operation involving a vessel and a helicopter is under way.
Romanian authorities did not say whether the fire was caused by a drone.
The incident occurred after Romania said on Wednesday, October 14, that it was investigating a possible new drone attack on a tanker off the Black Sea coast.
Rescuers rushed to assist the Comoros-flagged vessel Yara J after a fire broke out, but the ship's crew managed to extinguish the blaze on their own.
"Regardless of whether the vessel was hit by a drone or not, an investigation is currently under way," the country's Defense Minister Radu Miruțe told Digi24.
"This is a matter of considerable seriousness, given that such incidents are occurring in Romanian territorial waters," he said.
Suspected Russian drones have struck several vessels off the coasts of Romania and neighboring Bulgaria since last week, the publication writes.
According to the Turkish Chamber of Shipping IMEAK, at least 163 civilian and commercial vessels were hit in the Black Sea during the first eight months of this year.
Meanwhile, on Wednesday, Bulgaria said that Russia was likely behind the drone attacks that struck four vessels in the Black Sea last week, sinking two of them, but it had been unable to prove Moscow's culpability.
Rescuers are still searching for 11 crew members who went missing after drone strikes sank two vessels on Tuesday, October 13, in Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone and adjacent waters, while five other crew members were rescued.
One of the vessels is registered in Guinea-Bissau, but the other, Chelsea-3, belongs to Ukraine, is registered in Odesa, and sails under the flag of Malta, a member of the European Union.
"It makes no sense for Ukraine to attack its own ships and crews, given that the outcome of all these attacks benefits Russia, and indeed, the logic points to that. The problem is that we cannot prove it," Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev told parliament.
On Tuesday, Radev summoned Russia's ambassador to Sofia, who said that she had no information from Russia's Defense Ministry but did not rule out the possibility that "these attacks are a provocation by a third party," the publication writes.
The Guinea-Bissau-flagged cargo vessel Dignity sank on Tuesday after it was hit by a military strike, the publication writes. Four sailors—three Syrian citizens and one Egyptian—were rescued and taken to the port of Varna, said district governor Mario Smarkov.
"All four appeared to be in relatively good condition and had not sustained injuries," he said. A fifth sailor was expected to arrive later on Wednesday.
Smarkov said that the search for the 11 missing crew members was continuing.
Bulgaria requested international assistance in investigating the strikes on commercial vessels, as well as NATO support in strengthening surveillance and control systems and response capabilities against drone attacks.
EU response
These incidents have once again drawn close attention to Europe's ability to protect shipping and critical infrastructure in the Black Sea, more than a year after the EU launched a strategy to strengthen security in the region.
When the Black Sea Security Strategy was presented in May 2025, EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas warned that the region was feeling the consequences of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
"The Black Sea region is the main target for hybrid actions. The European Union seeks to strengthen cooperation in combating cyberattacks, disinformation, and other hostile actions," she said.
"Repeated violations of airspace and attacks on ports and shipping routes underscore this reality," she noted.
The policy was aimed at ensuring the security of this maritime corridor, as well as protecting critical infrastructure and assets such as offshore installations and underwater cables.
It also pledged to establish a Black Sea Maritime Security Center aimed at coordinating support and strengthening coast guard cooperation, among other activities.
The center will also analyze data from seafloor sensors and warn allies about potential dangers and future threats.

China launches eight AI computing satellites among 10 sent into orbit
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-15
07:43:07 UTC
16:43:07 KST

China has successfully launched 10 satellites aboard a Zhuque-2E Y4 carrier rocket, including eight designed to advance artificial intelligence computing capabilities in orbit, state-run Xinhua News Agency reported on Wednesday.
The rocket lifted off at 7.40 pm local time (1140 GMT) from the Dongfeng commercial space innovation pilot zone in northwestern China, placing all 10 satellites into their designated orbits, according to Xinhua.
Eight of the satellites belong to the second group of the Star Compute project, developed by Chinese commercial aerospace company ADAspace.
Designed to operate in dawn-dusk orbits, the satellites carry high-performance computing systems, laser communication equipment and low-light cameras.
They will test technologies including 10,000-watt liquid-cooling systems, large deployable cooling structures, space-based laser communication networks and the training of AI foundation models directly in orbit.
ADAspace said the mission would accelerate technological development and commercial applications of space-based computing.
Plans for orbital AI network
The company aims to establish an orbital AI infrastructure network comprising 2,800 computing satellites.
The first group of 12 satellites was launched in May 2025. In January, ADAspace announced that it had deployed Alibaba’s Qwen3 AI model aboard its orbital computing network, enabling AI processing directly in space.
The company plans to establish a 1,000-satellite network by 2030 and complete the larger constellation by 2035.

AFP has contacted the Pentagon for comment.

‘High likelihood of attack’: Israel set to extend home front emergency past election
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-15
07:37:44 UTC
16:37:44 KST

The Israeli government is expected to approve an extension of the nationwide special home front situation until November 3, keeping the emergency declaration in effect through the October 27 Knesset election amid security assessments warning of a continued high likelihood of an attack on the civilian population.
Defense Minister Israel Katz has requested the extension, which would prolong the declaration beyond its current October 20 expiration date. Government Secretary Yossi Fuchs circulated the proposal to ministers Thursday for approval in an urgent telephone vote.
According to the explanatory document accompanying the proposal, security officials believe there is still a "high likelihood" of an attack targeting civilians, particularly because of continued uncertainty surrounding the security situation with Iran and Lebanon.
The document also states that the need for any further extension will be reviewed before the new expiration date, based on an updated security assessment.
The government's decision will require approval from the Knesset's Foreign Affairs and Defense Committee.
Katz first declared a special home front situation across Israel on February 28, 2026, when Operation Roaring Lion against Iran began. The declaration has since been extended repeatedly through government decisions, most recently on October 6, when ministers approved its continuation until October 20.
Under Israeli law, a special home front situation grants the IDF's Home Front Command additional powers to issue emergency instructions to civilians, including restrictions on educational activities and public gatherings.
However, no such restrictions are currently in effect, meaning the proposed extension would preserve the authorities' ability to impose them if the security situation deteriorates rather than immediately introducing new limitations on daily life.
The extension would also mean that the nationwide emergency declaration remains in force on election day, as Israel prepares to vote amid continued concerns about possible attacks on the civilian population.
The Defense Ministry's legal adviser, attorney Mor Yamin-Bartal, determined that there is no legal obstacle to approving the proposal.
She acknowledged that repeatedly extending an emergency declaration that has remained in force since February could raise legal difficulties, but emphasized the urgency and necessity of the measure.

Source: Dubenko's cousin Anna Danylenko in a comment to Ukrainska Pravda.Zhyttia (Life)
Quote: "Today, the Russian world came to our family too. All those horrific photos from Lisovyi show my brother's section of the building. Those close to me know that I have two brothers. My cousin Andrii Dubenko has helped many people as a volunteer, dentist, medic and simply as someone who can fix almost anything. But now he's the one who needs help."
Details: Anna said her brother, his fiancée and their 72-year-old aunt were in the flat at the time of the strike. They survived because they followed the two-wall rule .
Rescue workers evacuated them using a rescue platform within 15 minutes of the attack.
The neighbouring apartment and the corridor were gutted by fire. All the windows in Andrii Dubenko's flat were blown out, while the blast wave damaged the rooms, completely destroying one of them. The force of the explosion was so powerful that it even ripped the linoleum from the floor.
"[My aunt] was comforting my brother's fiancée and telling her that we should not dwell on the past but look to the future.
We didn't sleep all night. We came back in the morning to clear the rubble because we hadn't been able to enter the apartment during the night – they were still putting out the fire. Everything is burnt, and there is a lot of water in the corridor, which was gutted by the fire. People are throwing broken belongings out of the windows onto the ground below. The smell of burning is everywhere," Anna said.
Among the debris, she gathered together the remains of a family tea set that they had used to drink tea from a samovar when their grandmother was still alive.
"It was my anchor, the anchor of our family," Anna wrote.
At the same time, a porcelain fish belonging to the family survived – reminiscent of the famous ceramic cockerel from Borodianka.
"Now we have our own 'fish of resilience' that has survived. Even my mother used to play with it. It was only on Monday that I was sitting in their cosy flat, where I grew up, and now I am looking through a hole that was a window just two days ago. [...]
It was painful to see injured people clearing out their homes – and, along with them, dismantling their lives," Anna said.
The family now needs help rebuilding their home. Anna has posted bank details on social media for those wishing to provide financial support.
Background: On 14 October, Russian forces struck a nine-storey residential building in the Lisovyi area of Kyiv's Desnianskyi district. The attack killed two people and injured 17 others.

UK economy grows 0.1% in August, defying contraction forecast
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-15
07:34:34 UTC
16:34:34 KST

Mucahithan Avcioglu
15 October 2026•Update: 15 October 2026
The UK economy grew 0.1% month-on-month in August, beating market expectations of a 0.1% contraction, according to Office for National Statistics data released Thursday.
Growth slowed from an unrevised 0.4% in July, while June's expansion was revised up to 0.4% from 0.3%.
Production output rose 0.8% in August, driving the monthly increase in gross domestic product (GDP), while services showed no growth and construction output fell 0.2%.
Manufacturing expanded 1.2%, with nine of its 13 subsectors recording growth. Pharmaceutical production rose 5.1%, providing the largest contribution to the manufacturing increase, followed by transport equipment, which grew 1.8%.
Mining and quarrying output increased 1.4%, while electricity and gas supply edged up 0.1%.
Within services, gains in wholesale and retail trade and professional, scientific and technical activities were offset by weakness elsewhere, including administrative and support services.
Consumer-facing services declined 0.3%, following a 0.1% fall in July. Sports, amusement and recreation activities dropped 7.1%, while food and beverage services fell 2.7%.
Construction output contracted for a fourth consecutive month, with new work falling 0.7%. Private housing new work declined 1.9%, contributing most to the monthly decrease.
 
3-month growth accelerates
GDP expanded 0.7% in the three months to August compared with the preceding three months, accelerating from 0.5% growth in the three months to July.
This marked the eighth consecutive increase on a rolling three-month basis.
Services grew 0.9%, providing the only positive contribution among the three main sectors. Production fell 0.2%, while construction declined 1%.
Professional, scientific and technical activities, alongside information and communication, supported services growth, with both subsectors expanding 2.8%.
The economy grew 2.1% compared with August last year. Over the three months to August, GDP was 1.8% higher than a year earlier.

Cosgrove was handed a two-game ban after being sent off in the closing stages of Auckland's 1-0 FIFA Intercontinental Cup loss to Saudi side Al-Ahli in August.
Auckland are allowed to play A-League professionals in their reserves side under New Zealand Football's participation agreement and competition regulations.
That includes up to two 23-year-old non-citizens for each match-day squad.
The clause opened the door for the 29-year-old Englishman to serve out his ban in Auckland's recent New Zealand National League fixtures against Wellington Olympic and Miramar Rangers.
In a fiery exchange on Thursday, Cosgrove could not recall the two matches and was bemused when asked if he had any unease or embarrassment over using the "loophole".
"Embarrassment?" he shot back at a reporter.
"Why would the club not push to have a player available and use every power that they have?"
Cosgrove bagged 11 goals in his debut season with Auckland, securing the men's competition golden boot along the way to the club's first championship.
"It doesn't matter, does it? I have technically [served my ban]. I've missed two NPL matches," Cosgrove said.
"If you pick up a suspension in the A-League, you have to serve it in the A-League.
"So technically, in that case, I should be missing the next few Intercontinental Cups, but I'm not."
The media conference ended abruptly before the reporter repeated his claim that Cosgrove had not actually served the ban.
"What are you doing here then? Bugger off, if you're going to talk shit," the striker replied.
An Auckland FC minder stated that FIFA, Football Australia and Football New Zealand were "fine" with the way the ban was served.
"You know what football's like in this country, mate? We f***ing work hard to get it good. You bring it down with shit like that," Cosgrove said, prompting a chuckle from the reporter.
"What are you laughing for? We'll just f*** you off. You won't get back here again."
In a podcast episode posted on Tuesday, Cosgrove said he was relieved when news of the rule's workaround became public so he could "finally stop lying about it".
"It was a poor challenge in oppressive heat and late in the game, but the two-game suspension was a little bit harsh," he told The Unused Subs podcast.
"We were trying to get that reduced, and the power of lawyers and legal teams these days, they managed to find a way to sign me up with the Auckland reserves."
The defending champions will begin their A-League campaign at home to Melbourne City on Saturday, before an away trip to face Western Sydney Wanderers on October 24.

A vase by Picasso’s daughter, Paloma Picasso, has been discovered at the charity shop in Bornem (Antwerp Province). The vintage vase dates from the 1990s and was used at the time to promote Paloma’s perfume. It is not clear how much it is worth. The vase will be auctioned via the charity shop’s website.
Christina, a member of staff at the Bornem charity shop, discovered the vase amongst the items that had been donated. “At first she thought it was a tourist trinket of little value, but when she took a closer look at the vase, she realised it was a vintage vase belonging to Pablo Picasso’s daughter, Paloma,” says Ann Doran of the social enterprise, which runs the charity shop in Bornem.
Paloma’s perfume
It is a vintage Greek vase featuring an image of the Minotaur – a monster, half-man, half-bull, from Greek mythology. “A matt ceramic vase that was used in the 1990s as promotional material for the launch of Paloma’s perfume, called ‘Minotaure’.”
The charity shop does not know how many were produced. “It is certainly a limited edition, even though they are copies of an original piece. It is a unique vintage find.”
Authentic piece
How does the charity shop know that a piece is authentic? “Our staff are trained by experts,” says Doran. “We work with art historian and auction expert Marcel Brouwer. Thanks to his tips and tricks, we’re able to recognise special pieces.”
“We’ve already sent Brouwer some photos; he’s certain it’s an authentic Paloma vase, but he’s coming here in a week’s time to examine it in person,” says Doran.
In the meantime, the vase has been set aside. The charity shop cannot estimate how much it is worth. It will be auctioned via the charity shop’s website.
It is also not known who brought the vase in, but it is not as though that person can now come and reclaim it. “What’s done is done,” says Doran with a laugh. She hopes the vase will fetch a tidy sum.

Catching Fog: How Architecture Collects Water from the Air
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-15
07:30:00 UTC
16:30:00 KST

Where rivers, reservoirs, and rainfall can no longer be relied upon consistently, water is increasingly being sought in the atmosphere. Fog, atmospheric humidity, and condensation each offer different ways of collecting it. When architecture begins to collect water from the air, surfaces, structures, and open spaces become part of the water system.
According to UNICEF, Jordan's National Water Strategy estimates that each person has access to only about 61 cubic meters of renewable water per year, far below the 500 cubic meters commonly used as a threshold for absolute water scarcity. Around half of the population receives piped water only once a week, while groundwater is being extracted faster than many aquifers can naturally recharge.
Atmospheric water harvesting encompasses several different technologies. Fog consists of suspended droplets that can be intercepted by mesh; dew forms when a surface cools below the dew point; and humidity can be extracted through sorption or condensation processes. Each requires different climatic conditions and produces different quantities of water. A critical review of atmospheric water harvesting for building façades identifies these as distinct approaches and finds that their integration into architecture remains constrained by technology readiness and manufacturing costs.
Related Article
Warka Water and Arturo Vittori Create Integrated Village for the Rainforest Community in Cameroon
Columbia GSAPP's Water Urbanism: Amman explored these possibilities in Jordan. Developed around Jordan's water crisis and refugee conditions, the studio proposed interventions that combined water collection with shade, sanitation, gathering, and productive landscapes. At the Al-Hadalat site, shelter clusters of refugees were proposed around fog towers capable of collecting an estimated 800 to 2,000 liters of water per day, alongside smaller shaded fog structures projected to collect around 500 liters. These figures are design projections rather than measured operational results.
Built from palm wood and mesh knitted from discarded ration sacks, the structure would intercept fog while using its exposure to moving air to provide shade and a place for congregation. Water would travel through the structure into underground storage before being distributed to showers, sanitation, and productive landscapes. Wastewater would move through constructed wetlands and return to the agricultural system.
Reservoirs, treatment plants and distribution networks operate largely outside the architectural experience of the city. Fog harvesting requires infrastructure to remain uncovered to the atmosphere. The collector must occupy space, remain exposed and respond directly to atmospheric conditions. Designing the collector as shade, shelter, or public space gives it another use.
Any such system still has to contend with the unpredictability of the atmosphere. Morocco provides an example where fog harvesting has moved beyond the speculative drawing into an operational water system. At Sidi Ifni, on the Atlantic coast, fog is collected at Boutmezguida mountain, approximately 35 meters inland from the coast, and channelled into a wider system serving local communities. A 2024 assessment of the project describes it as the world's largest fog-collection project and evaluates its water output, water quality and community participation.
The project's output varies substantially across the year. Over four years, annual average collection ranged between 1.6 and 6 liters per square metre per day. During the fog season, March and April produced an average of 8.5 liters per square metre per day, while the highest monthly figure recorded was 21 liters per square meter per day in April 2021. Fog occurred throughout the year, but its frequency varied, making storage and supplementary supply important to the system.
Collection is only one component of the system. Water has to be captured, stored, treated, and distributed. The community also has to participate in maintaining and using the infrastructure. The researchers identify fog-yield variability and groundwater pollution among the project's principal challenges, warning that relying on fog as the sole source could result in inconsistent water availability.
Research into atmospheric water harvesting on building façades suggests that the envelope could become an active collection surface. Orientation, surface area, material properties and exposure to air all become environmental design variables. Sorption-based systems, in particular, have been identified as promising for integration into building envelopes, although current research still identifies low technology-readiness and manufacturing costs as significant barriers.
A water-harvesting façade would sit between interior and exterior while also responding to air movement and collecting water from the surrounding atmosphere. Roofs could become condensation surfaces. Screens could become fog collectors. Courtyards could incorporate collection and storage. Structures could also provide shade where their collection systems need to remain exposed.
Architecture cannot design the atmosphere itself. It can orient a collector toward prevailing fog, increase its surface area, provide storage and reduce dependence on distant infrastructure. It cannot guarantee that fog will arrive. In practice, atmospheric water would need to operate alongside storage, treatment and conventional supply systems.
At Al-Hadalat, the fog tower combines collection with shade and gathering space. At Sidi Ifni, collection forms part of a larger system of storage, treatment and distribution. At the building scale, façades can collect water while continuing to control heat, light and air.
Architecture has always responded to the atmosphere: keeping rain out, tempering heat, admitting daylight and directing air. Atmospheric water harvesting adds another task: collecting water from the same atmospheric conditions buildings already respond to. Atmospheric water harvesting works as part of a wider water network. It adds another source to that network, one whose performance depends on climate, exposure, storage, and maintenance.
This article is part of the ArchDaily Topic: The Architecture of Water: Territories, Tensions & Transformations. Across China: When yak milk meets coffee on China's Tibetan plateau
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-15
15:23:33 CST
16:23:33 KST

This file photo shows Gonbu at a coffee shop in Songpan County, southwest China's Sichuan Province.(Xinhua)
CHENGDU, Oct. 15 (Xinhua) -- Gonbu never developed a taste for coffee, and that remains true to this day.
But that hasn't stopped the 30-year-old Tibetan from opening a restaurant that serves coffee with a local twist: yak milk, highland barley and butter.
Growing up on the grasslands of southwest China's Sichuan Province, Gonbu spent his childhood days riding horses and herding yaks. He had never even heard of coffee.
Today, he is bringing the flavors of his childhood to visitors in the ancient town of Songpan, hoping to ignite interest in the nomadic culture behind them.
Gonbu runs a Tibetan restaurant in the town, which has a history spanning over 1,000 years. Located in Songpan County, where the average elevation exceeds 3,000 meters, the town was once a trading hub between southwestern and northwestern China. There, traders exchanged horses, medicinal herbs, and animal hides for tea and grain.
Born in Caoyuan Village in Songpan's Maoergai Township, he later studied Tibetan-Chinese translation at Northwest Minzu University in Lanzhou, where he tried coffee for the first time.
He was drawn to the atmosphere of coffee shops -- "somewhere you can read a book or just sit for a while," as he put it.
He found similar places in other cities and wondered why the grasslands couldn't have one, too.
In 2019, Gonbu returned to Maoergai and opened a small reading lounge serving coffee. "Young people on the grasslands also need somewhere to relax and learn about the outside world," he said.
Over the next five years, he traveled to learn coffee-making and Tibetan cooking while studying how restaurants operated in cities.
He kept thinking about Songpan's ancient town. The county is a gateway to the UNESCO World Heritage sites of Jiuzhai Valley and Huanglong, and the town now has more than 10 businesses established by returning college graduates.
In late 2024, Gonbu opened the restaurant, hoping to offer visitors a fresh perspective on Tibetan cuisine and nomadic life.
Inside, sheepskins are draped over the chairs, and ingredients are sourced from the plateau whenever possible. Traditional Tibetan dishes share the menu with coffee made from barley, yak milk, butter and yak yogurt.
By day, customers eat, drink coffee and read. In the evening, traditional ethnic music alternates with modern folk songs.
Gonbu wants the restaurant to offer more than just food and entertainment. He teaches his staff to make coffee and has filled the restaurant with books.
Of his 18 employees, 12 come from Maoergai. Their average age is just 22 to 23.
One is 18-year-old Tsering Drolkar. Had she not come to the ancient town, she said, she would probably be herding yaks at home. Collecting medicinal herbs can sometimes bring in good money.
"I just want to go out and see more of the world," she said. Since arriving, she has learned to make coffee, played the guitar for the first time and encountered unfamiliar foods.
At 11, she traveled beyond the grasslands for the first time, visiting her father's hometown of Mianyang in Sichuan. Before the trip, she had heard stories of watermelons, bananas and other fruits rarely seen back home.
Today, leaving the remote highlands is easier. Nine decades ago, crossing them was a struggle for survival.
In 1935, the Communist Party of China-led Red Army entered northwest Sichuan during the Long March, a roughly 12,500-kilometer military odyssey from 1934 to 1936. The soldiers crossed the marshy grasslands of what are now Songpan, Hongyuan, Ruoergai and surrounding areas.
In his book "The Long March: The Untold Story," American journalist and author Harrison Salisbury described the area as "untouched for 3,000 years." With its swamps, extreme cold and low oxygen levels, the treacherous terrain claimed the lives of many soldiers.
This year marks the 90th anniversary of the Long March's victory. Gonbu's grandparents lived through that era and passed down stories of the Red Army.
"With transportation being so convenient today, it's really hard to imagine what they went through back then," he said.
On Aug. 30, 2024, a new section of the Sichuan-Qinghai railway opened, bringing bullet train services to Songpan. From Huanglong-Jiuzhai station, a short drive from the ancient town, the fastest trains reach Chengdu in about one hour and 40 minutes.
Near the station stands a memorial park commemorating the Long March. A statue depicts a Red Army soldier raising a rifle and flowers. Nearby, modern trains speed past.
The grasslands are now drawing more visitors. Songpan County received 10.64 million tourist visits in 2025, up 15.53 percent year on year, with total tourism spending reaching 31.81 billion yuan (about 4.73 billion U.S. dollars).
Visitors now come for more than scenery. They ride horses, hike, watch the stars or stop for coffee in the ancient town. The shift toward experiencing local life reflects the growing popularity of immersive tourism in China.
The outline of China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030), released in March, calls for closer integration of culture and tourism and a wider range of high-quality tourism offerings.
For Gonbu, a cup of yak milk coffee is only a starting point. If customers wonder where the milk comes from, he hopes to take them to Maoergai to see the yaks, pastures and people who produce it.
He plans to build a ranch there with a reading lounge, bringing together food, tourism and herding life.
"Tradition and modernity, the countryside and the city -- they can all come together in a place like this," he said. ■

Across China: Jurassic fossil found in east China challenges assumptions about early bird evolution
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-15
15:23:24 CST
16:23:24 KST

This undated file photo shows the site where the fossilized Yuezhuornis yangyuanensis is discovered, in Zhenghe County, east China's Fujian Province. A newly unearthed Jurassic fossil from east China is prompting scientists to rethink one of the most basic assumptions about bird evolution: that early birds always evolved toward better flight capability. The 150-million-year-old bird, named Yuezhuornis yangyuanensis, was about the size of a crow and lived during the Late Jurassic period. The fossil was found in Zhenghe County, east China's Fujian Province. What makes this bird so surprising is not how well it flew, but the fact that it likely did not fly at all. The fossil was discovered by researchers from the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology (IVPP) of the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) and the Fujian Institute of Geological Sciences, and has been described in a study published in the journal Nature. (Xinhua)
BEIJING, Oct. 15 (Xinhua) -- A newly unearthed Jurassic fossil from east China is prompting scientists to rethink one of the most basic assumptions about bird evolution: that early birds always evolved toward better flight capability.
The 150-million-year-old bird, named Yuezhuornis yangyuanensis, was about the size of a crow and lived during the Late Jurassic period. The fossil was found in Zhenghe County, east China's Fujian Province. What makes this bird so surprising is not how well it flew, but the fact that it likely did not fly at all.
The fossil was discovered by researchers from the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology (IVPP) of the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) and the Fujian Institute of Geological Sciences, and has been described in a study published in the journal Nature.
According to the study, Yuezhuornis is the earliest known example of a bird losing the ability to fly. Some parts of its body look like those of a bird, such as its pelvic and hindlimb elements. But it also retained traits from its dinosaur ancestors, including closely packed, serrated teeth and a special second toe that is highly extensible. These features are usually found in deinonychosaurs, not in birds.
Through their analysis, the researchers found that the limb proportions of Yuezhuornis were similar to those of living ground-dwelling birds and some non-avialan paravians, pointing to a terrestrial, flightless lifestyle.
"When we examined Yuezhuornis, we were struck by its extraordinary mix of features," said Wang Min, corresponding author of the study and a researcher at the IVPP. "It shows us that early bird evolution was far more complicated than we previously realized."
To figure out where this puzzling species belonged on the evolutionary tree, the research team ran a series of detailed analyses, using two different methods to compare its traits with those of other early birds and their relatives.
"The results consistently placed Yuezhuornis firmly within the Avialae, the group that includes modern birds and their closest extinct relatives. To put it simply, it sits on the evolutionary tree just above Archaeopteryx, the famous early bird from Germany. This means Yuezhuornis is slightly closer to modern birds than Archaeopteryx is. It is also the sister taxon to Zhengheornis, another early bird found at the same fossil site in Fujian, which means the two share a common ancestor and are each other's closest relatives on that branch," said Zhou Zhonghe, a co-author of the study and an academician of the CAS.
According to Wang, the discovery of a flightless, ground-dwelling bird from the Late Jurassic challenges the idea that flight was the main force driving early bird evolution. Instead, it suggests that some early birds followed evolutionary paths that did not favor flight, highlighting the remarkable ecological and morphological diversity that emerged during the early evolution of birds.
Meanwhile, Wang noted that the continuing discovery of early avialans underscores the potential of the Zhenghe Fauna to shed light on a poorly documented chapter of Jurassic bird evolution.
The Zhenghe Fauna is a terrestrial biota evidenced by a large number of tortoise, turtle, fish and plant fossils that have been unearthed. It is known as the southernmost location globally where avialan fossils from the late Jurassic Period are preserved.
During the late Jurassic Period, frequent volcanic eruptions occurred along the region's southeastern coastline. However, during quiescent periods, lakes and basins formed in the mountainous areas of what is today called Zhenghe County, creating a favorable ecological environment for plant growth and animal habitation.
Experts believe that Zhenghe's unique biological composition and geological background provide important information for the study of the evolution of terrestrial ecosystems in the late Jurassic Period, as well as the origins of birds and other animals. ■

SEOUL, Oct. 15 (Xinhua) -- South Korea's household loan growth at banks slowed last month due to a cooldown in stock and property markets, central bank data showed Thursday.
Debt owed by households to deposit-taking banks totaled 1,198.9 trillion won (about 889.6 billion U.S. dollars) at the end of September, up 0.6 trillion won from a month earlier, according to the Bank of Korea (BOK).
It marked a significant slowdown from the previous month's 3.5 trillion won increase.
The slowdown was caused by a slump in retail stock investments and a reduction in newly completed housing.
Other loans, including credit loans, credit lines, and commercial real estate-backed loans, decreased by 2.3 trillion won in September from a month earlier, after a 0.6 trillion won decline in August.
Mortgage loans grew 2.9 trillion won last month, but the increase was smaller than the 4.1 trillion won expansion in the prior month.
The number of move-ins of newly built apartments across the country fell to 14,000 in September from 19,000 in the previous month.
Corporate loans extended by domestic banks totaled 1,441.5 trillion won at the end of September, up 10.7 trillion won from a month earlier, compared with a 9.7 trillion won rise the previous month.
Lending to large corporations rose by 7.5 trillion won, while loans to small and medium-sized enterprises increased by 3.2 trillion won in September. ■
